title: Spending Employer Allowance against a Till Transaction on an Employee Meal Account
content:
Where employer allowance stands on an Employee Meal Account and a till transaction has already been rung against payroll, the allowance may be spent against that transaction so that part of the meal is met by the employer rather than by the employee. This page governs that spending.

The allowance applied to a till transaction is not settled before the allowance lot the account is owed for the current grant period stands on its ledger.

## What it governs and what it books

What is governed here is the employer allowance spent against one till transaction. One application entry is booked for the whole of the allowance applied to a till transaction, whatever lots it draws on, and the unspent employer allowance standing on the account comes down by the same value; the employee sees that meal part met by the employer rather than by them.

## Booking it

The desk unlocks the agent tool `apply_allowance_to_ticket_3fbfdeca` and calls it. The call books an allowance application entry on the account's transaction ledger for the value stated and marks it with the till transaction it meets.

### Parameters

| Parameter | What it is | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `meal_account_id` | The reference number of the Employee Meal Account whose allowance is being spent | An account reference, read from the meal account lookup before the call |
| `applied_amount_usd` | The employer allowance spent against that till transaction, in USD | Recorded to 2 decimal places and rounded half to even at that precision; stored as a positive magnitude; an empty value is not accepted |
| `original_pos_reference` | The till transaction the allowance is applied to | Written as POS- followed by 8 digits exactly as it is printed on that transaction in the account's activity; an empty value is not accepted |

### What comes back

A plain confirmation sentence naming the reference of the allowance application booked, the value applied in USD to two decimal places, the till transaction it was applied to and the unspent employer allowance left standing. The presence of that application reference is what indicates the allowance was spent.

## Basis Q&A

**Whose action is this?** The desk's own; the tool is an agent tool, unlocked and called by the agent handling the account.

**How many entries does one application make?** One, for the whole of the allowance applied to that till transaction.
